form.label: MITRE ATT&CK
form.description: Which adversary techniques the fleet's open vulnerabilities could enable.

div.b: Read this as exposure, not as attack evidence.
div.span: The chain is CVE → CWE → CAPEC → ATT&CK technique, and every hop is a mapping MITRE publishes. But it is many-to-many and lossy: it says this weakness class is the kind of thing that enables that technique, not that an adversary used it, and not that this particular vulnerability is exploitable in your environment. A CVE with no CWE, or a CWE MITRE has not mapped, simply does not appear — so absence here is not safety. Use it to see which capabilities your open findings could hand an attacker, and pair it with the KEV and EPSS columns on Findings, which are about real-world exploitation rather than classification.

panel.title: ATT&CK matrix — where open findings sit in an attack

search.query: | `riskability_attack_matrix` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ $conf_tok$ | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY tactic_name, tactic_order, technique_name | eventstats max(cves) AS peak BY technique_name | sort - peak | head 120 | sort tactic_order | fields tactic_name, technique_name, cves

viz.option: No tactic data. The matrix needs the ATT&CK tactic mapping, which older feed bundles do not carry — rebuild the bundle with --mitre and import it. Until then this panel is blank because the mapping is missing, not because nothing is exposed.

div.b: An empty matrix is not a clean matrix.
div.span: The grid needs MITRE's technique-to-tactic mapping, which only bundles built with --mitre by a recent feed builder carry. If this panel is empty, rebuild the bundle and import it — the techniques listed below are still correct in the meantime, they simply cannot be placed in an attack sequence without tactics. Cells show distinct CVEs; a technique appears in every tactic MITRE assigns it, so reading across a row counts the same CVEs more than once.

panel.title: Techniques enabled by open findings, most exposed first

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ $conf_tok$ | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves, dc(hostname) AS hosts, dc(package) AS packages, values(cwe) AS weaknesses, max(epss) AS peak_epss BY technique, technique_name | eval peak_epss = round(peak_epss, 4) | sort - cves | rename technique AS "Technique", technique_name AS "Name", cves AS "CVEs", hosts AS "Hosts", packages AS "Packages", weaknesses AS "Via CWE", peak_epss AS "Peak EPSS"

viz.option: No open finding maps to a technique. Most CVEs carry no CWE, so this is usually a gap in the mapping rather than an absence of exposure.

panel.title: Weakness classes present in the fleet (CWE)

search.query: | `riskability_finding_cwes` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | search $cwe_filter$ | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY cwe | sort - cves | head 40

viz.option: No open finding carries a CWE. Most CVEs have no recorded weakness class, so this is a gap in the mapping rather than an absence of risk — see the coverage panel beside it.

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | lookup riskability_advisory_lookup cve_id OUTPUT cwes | eval mapped = case(isnull(cwes) OR cwes=="", "no CWE recorded for this CVE", 1=1, "has a CWE") | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY mapped | eventstats sum(cves) AS total | eval share = round(cves*100/total, 1)."%" | fields mapped, cves, share | rename mapped AS "Mapping status", cves AS "CVEs", share AS "Share"

viz.option: Nothing to summarise: there are no open findings to classify.

panel.title: Which weaknesses lead to which techniques — $tech_label$

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ $conf_tok$ | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | stats dc(cve_id) AS cves BY cwe, technique_name | sort - cves | head 25

viz.option: Nothing to map. No open finding has a CWE that MITRE links to a technique.

div.b: Widths do not add up, by design.
div.span: One weakness can enable several techniques, so a single CVE is drawn once per technique it reaches. Each ribbon is honest on its own — that many distinct CVEs connect that CWE to that technique — but summing the right-hand side counts the same CVE several times. Read concentration, not totals. Only the top 25 links are shown.

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ $conf_tok$ | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | stats min(epss) AS lo, perc25(epss) AS q1, median(epss) AS med, perc75(epss) AS q3, max(epss) AS hi, dc(cve_id) AS cves BY technique_name | where cves >= 3 | sort - cves | head 15 | fields technique_name, lo, q1, med, q3, hi

viz.option: Not enough scored CVEs per technique to show a distribution. EPSS comes from the feed; if it was not included in the bundle there is nothing to plot.

div.b: Why a distribution rather than a peak.
div.span: The table above reports each technique's highest EPSS, which one noisy CVE can dominate. A box shows whether a technique is backed by many likely-exploited CVEs or by a single outlier — those call for different responses. Techniques with fewer than three scored CVEs are omitted as too small to describe.
Click a technique, a matrix cell, a CWE tile, a Sankey ribbon or a box below to narrow this page to it.
This page is narrowed. The panels below show only what matches; the matrix and the technique list stay whole so you can pick something else.

These are the findings that put this technique on the matrix. Every one is a real vulnerability; the technique is what MITRE says this class of weakness could enable, not something anyone observed. Read the technique on attack.mitre.org (needs internet).

search.query: | `riskability_attack_surface` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ $conf_tok$ | search $tech_filter$ $cwe_filter$ | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | eval installed_version = last_version | table technique, technique_name, cve_id, package, installed_version, fixed_version, hostname, root, cwe, via_capec, epss | sort technique, - epss | rename technique AS "Technique", technique_name AS "Name", cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", installed_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", hostname AS "Host", root AS "Root", cwe AS "CWE", via_capec AS "Via CAPEC", epss AS "EPSS"

viz.option: No findings map to a technique at the current confidence filter.
